name: Reviews
summary: Walk a set of goals together on a cadence, decide what happens next and keep what was said.

rebuild.builds: Reviews, as a feature a workspace can switch off. A review walks a set of goals together on a cadence (every 1, 2 or 4 weeks, on a weekday): its agenda puts the goals that need attention first, worst and stalest, and the walk opens each goal's page in turn, where someone in the review marks it reviewed, adds a note, asks the owner a question, agrees a next step with who and by when, or accepts the risk on a goal behind; a goal off track or at risk leaves the walk with a decision. What was said stays on each goal: questions and next steps are asks, open on the owner's Home until answered or done; a held session leads its page with what was said, and prints. Off, Reviews has no menu row or phone tab, no page (its addresses say it is switched off and who can switch it on), no Next review on Home, no Last time we talked or walk on a goal, no review tools for an assistant and no review asked for on Workspace; asks and next steps stay as they are, History keeps what was said, and switching it back on brings every review back as it was. An admin switches it off on Workspace, Features, after a read-back that counts what stays.
entry: The core rules (stage 1) work out each goal's status, flags and attention, and the asks (stage 1: one way to ask): a review reads them and adds nothing to them.
The core keeps a workspace's switched-off modules (Workspace.modulesOff) and refuses a switched-off module's actions and AI tools (stage 2).
exit: Switched off, the menu has no Reviews row and the phone's tabs are Home, Check-in, Goals and People for someone with a goal to check in on, and Home, Goals, People and Activity for anyone else (the two rows of navigation.csv at the address “/ (Reviews off)”).

Switched off, every review address shows Page not found with “Reviews is switched off in {workspace}. An admin can switch it on in Workspace, Features.”, a goal's address with ?review= opens the goal without it, and the six review actions and tools refuse with “Reviews is off in {workspace}.” or the switched-off module's sentence (check N21).

Switched off, Home has no Next review cell and no review lead: someone who owns no goal is led to the goals they watch that need attention (“Goals you watch · {n} need attention · See them”), or to nothing; a question waits by its own age and names no session; the due flag says “Due by Thu 12 Nov.”, on or off.

Switching off first reads back what stays (the reviews, what was said in them, the open next steps and questions raised in one) from the rule switchOffReadBack, and Undo brings Reviews back (journey U103).
Back on, every review, its people, its cadence and what was said are as they were (journey U104).

The clock's words come from one rule, dueWords (rule RS1), and match every row of spec/conformance/reviews.csv: “before Thursday’s review” only with Reviews on and a review held on the due day, otherwise “by Thursday”; switched off, no page names a review in its own words outside Workspace, Features, History's unlinked names and the closed page's sentence, and the check-in's receipt says “…checked in for week 45, by Thursday.” (journey U148).

A closed page says “Reviews is switched off in {workspace}. An admin can switch it on in Workspace, Features.”, and every review tool, and edit_call on a note said in a review, answers “Reviews is switched off in {workspace}, so {tool} can’t be used there. An admin can switch it on in Workspace, under Features.”, the one sentence every switched-off module's tools use (check N30).

The read-back before switching off adds, after the questions line, “{n} accepted risks stay on their goals, as they were said. No new one can be accepted while Reviews is off.” (left out at nought) and “Check-ins are still due by Thursday. “Before the review” becomes “by Thursday” on Home, in the check-in and in the count of goals checked in on time.” (rule RS2; the readback row of reviews.csv).

Switched off, the workbook has no Notes sheet and no Review column on Asks; a workbook that has them loads as usual, and the preview says once “Reviews is off in {workspace}: the Notes sheet and the Review column were not read.”.
Switched back on after a week off, every session whose date passed while it was off moves to its next date: neither Reviews nor Home says “Not held yet” (journey U149).
gaps: Reviews is a switch, not yet a folder of its own (FT3 moves it): its screens (src/screens/Review.tsx, src/screens/Inspect.tsx, ReviewPrint in src/screens/Print.tsx), its rules (src/domain/review.ts, with offSpell for a session passed while it was off; src/domain/reviewsOff.ts, the read-back's switchOffReadBack; src/domain/decide.ts, the review half of src/domain/onePager.ts, lastTalked in src/domain/goalPage.ts), its actions (saveReview, reviewCall, acceptRisk, markReviewed, unmarkReviewed, endReview and deleteReview in src/domain/actions.ts and src/domain/removal.ts), its menu row (src/domain/navigation.ts) and its table (okr_reviews, migration 0006, with review_id on okr_decisions and okr_requests) are still the core's. Its review actions refuse while it is off in src/app/actions.ts (performAny), and the read-back sheet is drawn by src/screens/Workspace.tsx. This folder holds its routes, its Help article and its AI tools; src/app/reads.ts reviewsOn is the one place that asks whether it is on.

A review's own records (reviews and what was said in them) are not yet declared as the module's (AS part 2's records extension point is FT3's), so a build without the module still loads and saves them as the core's.

The walk on a goal's page, Home's review lead and its Next review cell are drawn by core screens, not through places; FT3 adds the places (home.lead, home.glance) and a count for a module's menu item.
